title: Add Waybar and Polybar integration guide and sample configs
description: Document how to integrate LAYA's `--stream` JSON output with Waybar and Polybar for tiling window manager status bars (Hyprland, Sway, i3).
pr_body:
## Summary

This PR adds comprehensive integration guides and ready-to-use configuration snippets for **Waybar** and **Polybar** under `docs/integrations/waybar-polybar.md`.

### Why this is needed
LAYA already supports the `--stream` flag for headless status bar output, but users had to guess the JSON schema and event triggers. Providing copy-paste configurations makes it trivial for r/unixporn, Hyprland, and Sway users to adopt LAYA immediately.

### Changes
- Created `docs/integrations/waybar-polybar.md` with Waybar `config.jsonc`, CSS styling, and Polybar `config.ini` examples.
- Documented JSON output schema and testing commands.

### Checklist
- [x] Tested Waybar module format compatibility
- [x] Verified JSON return fields (`text`, `alt`, `tooltip`, `class`)
- [x] Clear documentation links

title: RFC 001: User configuration file support (~/.config/laya/config.toml)
description: Specify the architecture and design for a user configuration file in TOML/YAML format to customize keybindings, lyric sources, and theme preferences.

files.docs/rfcs/001-user-configuration.md:
# RFC 001: User Configuration File Support

- **Status**: Proposed
- **Author**: Sahas Timilsina
- **Created**: 2026-09-24

## Context & Problem Statement

LAYA currently relies on hardcoded keybindings (e.g. Vim keys `j`, `k`, `l`, space), default animation rates, and automatic theme extraction. Users with non-QWERTY keyboard layouts, alternative color schemes, or specific player preferences (e.g., prioritize `spotify` over `firefox`) cannot persist their preferences.

## Proposed Solution

Introduce a configuration loader that reads from standard XDG paths:
1. `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/laya/config.toml`
2. Falling back to `~/.config/laya/config.toml`

### Proposed Schema (`config.toml`)

```toml
[general]
default_player = "spotify"
refresh_rate_ms = 250
auto_theme = true

[keybindings]
play_pause = "space"
next_track = ["n", "right"]
prev_track = ["p", "left"]
toggle_lyrics = "l"
seek_forward = "]"
seek_backward = "["
quit = ["q", "ctrl+c"]

[lyrics]
prefer_local_lrc = true
enable_lrclib_fallback = true
cache_directory = "~/.cache/laya/lyrics"

[theme]
border_style = "rounded" # "rounded", "normal", "double", "thick"
accent_color = "#89b4fa"
background_color = "#1e1e2e"
```

## Implementation Plan

1. Use `BurntSushi/toml` or `pelletier/go-toml/v2` for zero-dependency TOML deserialization.
2. Create `internal/config/config.go` with `Config` struct and sensible defaults.
3. Integrate `config` into Bubble Tea model initialization in `app/app.go`.

pr_body:
## Summary

This PR introduces **RFC 001: User Configuration File Support**, detailing the architecture, XDG file paths, and schema for `~/.config/laya/config.toml`.

### Motivation
Allowing users to customize keybindings, player priorities, and lyric caches makes LAYA significantly more accessible and adaptable to different window managers and user workflows.

### Discussion Points
- Should we prefer TOML or YAML? (TOML is recommended for terminal tools like Alacritty, Starship, Helix).
- Validation of keybinding strings in Bubble Tea (`tea.KeyMsg`).

title: Add XDG desktop entry and Arch Linux PKGBUILD spec
description: Add standard XDG desktop entry and Arch Linux PKGBUILD template to enable installation via AUR or desktop app launchers.

files.packaging/laya.desktop:
[Desktop Entry]
Type=Application
Name=LAYA
GenericName=Media Controller
Comment=Terminal-based MPRIS media controller and dashboard
Exec=laya
Icon=multimedia-player
Terminal=true
Categories=AudioVideo;Audio;Player;ConsoleOnly;
Keywords=music;mpris;media;player;tui;
files.packaging/PKGBUILD:
# Maintainer: Sahas Timilsina <contact@sahas.me>
pkgname=laya-git
pkgver=0.1.0
pkgrel=1
pkgdesc="Terminal-based MPRIS media controller and dashboard built with Go and Bubble Tea"
arch=('x86_64' 'aarch64')
url="https://github.com/Sahas001/laya"
license=('MIT')
depends=('glibc')
makedepends=('go' 'git')
provides=('laya')
conflicts=('laya')
source=("${pkgname}::git+https://github.com/Sahas001/laya.git")
sha256sums=('SKIP')

build() {
  cd "${srcdir}/${pkgname}"
  export CGO_ENABLED=0
  export GOFLAGS="-trimpath -mod=readonly -modcacherw"
  go build -ldflags="-s -w" -o laya main.go
}

package() {
  cd "${srcdir}/${pkgname}"
  install -Dm755 laya "${pkgdir}/usr/bin/laya"
  install -Dm644 packaging/laya.desktop "${pkgdir}/usr/share/applications/laya.desktop"
  install -Dm644 README.md "${pkgdir}/usr/share/doc/${pkgname}/README.md"
}

pr_body:
## Summary

This PR adds standard Linux packaging assets:
1. `packaging/laya.desktop` — Allows application launchers (Rofi, Wofi, Fuzzel, GNOME) to discover and launch LAYA in a terminal window.
2. `packaging/PKGBUILD` — Ready for submission to the Arch User Repository (AUR) as `laya-git`.

### Review Notes
- Validated `laya.desktop` against `desktop-file-validate` standards.
- Clean `CGO_ENABLED=0` build instructions for static binary distribution.

title: RFC 002: Dynamic visualizer modes and audio spectrum rendering
description: Design specification for pluggable visualizer display modes in LAYA (Sine wave, Block columns, Braille curve).

files.docs/rfcs/002-visualizer-customization.m:
# RFC 002: Dynamic Visualizer Modes & Audio Spectrum Rendering

- **Status**: Proposed
- **Author**: Sahas Timilsina
- **Created**: 2026-09-24

## Context & Objective

LAYA includes a stylish wave visualizer in the main dashboard view. Currently, the wave generator uses a fixed mathematical sine/cosine interpolation. Users have requested multiple visualizer styles:
1. **Waveform (Current)**: Smooth horizontal undulating wave.
2. **Block Columns / Frequency Bars**: Traditional equalizer columns (` ▂▃▄▅▆▇█`).
3. **Braille Curves**: Ultra-high-density dots using Unicode 2800..28FF Braille characters.

## Architecture

Define a `Visualizer` interface in `ui/visualizer.go`:

```go
type VisualizerMode string

const (
    ModeSineWave VisualizerMode = "wave"
    ModeBars     VisualizerMode = "bars"
    ModeBraille  VisualizerMode = "braille"
)

type Visualizer interface {
    Render(width, height int, tick int64, isPlaying bool) string
}
```

## Keybinding Integration

Pressing `v` in the dashboard will cycle through available modes:
`Wave -> Bars -> Braille -> Hidden`.

pr_body:
## Summary

This PR proposes **RFC 002: Dynamic Visualizer Modes**, introducing a clean interface pattern for visualizer algorithms in the Bubble Tea UI.

### Benefits
- Enables users to switch between sine wave, equalizer bars, and Braille density curves with a single keypress (`v`).
- Prepares LAYA for optional FIFO / CAVA audio feed integration in the future.

title: RFC 003: Vim-style command bar and quick player switching
description: Design specification for interactive `:` command mode in LAYA for power users.

files.docs/rfcs/003-command-bar.md:
# RFC 003: Vim-Style Command Bar & Interactive Commands

- **Status**: Proposed
- **Author**: Sahas Timilsina
- **Created**: 2026-09-24

## Overview

To enhance power user efficiency, LAYA will support an interactive command line activated by pressing `:`.

### Commands

- `:player <name>`: Switch active MPRIS player directly (e.g. `:player spotify` or `:player mpv`).
- `:seek <+/-seconds>`: Seek forward or backward by specific duration.
- `:theme <dark|light|auto>`: Manually override or reset theme mode.
- `:lyrics <reload|toggle>`: Force reload lyrics from local or remote LRCLIB.
- `:quit` or `:q`: Gracefully exit.

### Component Design

Integrates Charm's `bubbles/textinput` component at the bottom border of the terminal viewport when in `StateCommand` mode.

pr_body:
## Summary

This PR proposes **RFC 003: Vim-Style Command Bar** for power users.

### Highlights
- Detailed state machine transition in Bubble Tea (`StateDashboard` <-> `StateCommand`).
- Tab-completion support for player names and command verbs.
